evidence.evidence_text: Method: We propose an Etiology-Aware Attention Supervision framework that introduces structured etiological information as an external supervisory signal for training large language models.

Specifically, we construct Clinical Etiology Schema (CES) derived from authoritative clinical guidelines for three acute abdominal conditions: acute appendicitis, acute pancreatitis, and acute cholecystitis.

Result: Experiments conducted on a Consistent Diagnosis Cohort demonstrate that the proposed framework improves average diagnostic accuracy by 15.65% compared with baseline models.
External evaluation on a Discrepant Diagnosis Cohort further confirms the robustness of diagnostic performance improvements under real-world clinical inconsistencies.
Based on CES annotations, we develop an Etiology-Aware Head Identification strategy to identify attention heads that consistently align with etiological evidence.

Building on this analysis, we design a structure-guided parameter-efficient fine-tuning approach that steers attention distributions toward clinically relevant evidence through an additional supervision loss, without modifying the base model architecture.
